teams.synopsis: A season-high 177.7 without even Amon-Ra — Hockenson and Geno Smith picked up the slack.
teams.blurb: A new number 1 once again — Brandon's team put up a season-high 177.7 points in Week 4. Despite not having Amon-Ra, Brandon was able to put up historic numbers for the PFFL. This could be attributed to Hockenson taking advantage of his teammate's ineligibility and Geno Smith being a formidable fantasy QB through 4 weeks. This team has the ability and the players to outperform every opponent for the foreseeable future, so look for Brandon to retain this spot next week and continue his hot streak.

teams.synopsis: A top-3 seed looks realistic — elite depth everywhere, and Brian Robinson's return could push it further.
teams.blurb: I hesitate to put myself at number 2, because I don't think ranking yourself high is a good look, but I truly believe this current team has the ability to grab a top-3 seed by the time the playoffs come. From head to toe, this team has everything you want: a top RB duo, two upper-tier WR2's, the best TE in fantasy football, and some promising bench pieces with the potential to be mid-tier flex options. That being said, this manager is always looking for trades around the PFFL. Also, note that <mark class="hl-player">Brian Robinson</mark>, a rookie RB for Washington, is returning this week after being shot in August. He was seen as the lead back before the season, so we'll see if that rings true these next couple of weeks.

teams.synopsis: Chasing a first-ever championship — Henry's heating up and Keenan's return could make this duo elite.
teams.blurb: Our last-week number 1 is now down two spots, but is hoping to regain his throne next week. After not finding success in the first two seasons of the PFFL, McQuaid looks to earn his first top-5 finish and, more importantly, his first championship. We still have a long way to go, but Ryan is making a very good case for the best team this season, led by <mark class="hl-player">Henry</mark> — who's come alive these past couple weeks — and <mark class="hl-player">Waddle</mark>. Pay attention to how Waddle plays without <mark class="hl-player">Tua</mark> this week, though; it may shrink his stock a little bit. Also, <mark class="hl-player">Keenan</mark> is supposed to make his return this week, which will make for an elite WR duo.

teams.synopsis: Elite top-to-bottom talent with Jalen Hurts at the helm — the highest projection in the league for Week 5.
teams.blurb: This is my vote for who I think will have the 1st seed in a couple months. Just so much star power on one team — an elite RB duo (7th and 10th ranked), two WR1's (10th and 14th ranked), and the 3rd-best QB in <mark class="hl-player">Jalen Hurts</mark>. This team doesn't have the glamour we all wanted in a top team at draft night, but it's filled with fantasy studs for the 2022 PFFL season. I don't have much more to say about this team, but I have a feeling it'll be in my top 2 next week, thanks to having the highest projection for Week 5.

teams.synopsis: The best QB in the league and a top-6 RB — a healthy Kamara makes this team downright scary.
teams.blurb: The only reason Max fell this week is because other teams had great weeks, while his team looked average (despite the win). I'm excited to see if this team can be consistent and play like a top-5 team week in and week out. He has the best fantasy QB this season, and if you combine that with the 6th-best RB and a solid trio of low-mid-tier WR2s, you get a very competitive team. Also, if <mark class="hl-player">Kamara</mark> comes back and plays like an RB1, the entire league should be scared of this team's capabilities.

teams.synopsis: 1-3 but unlucky — a big swing for Chubb should turn this record around soon.
teams.blurb: I know this team is 1-3, but if you look into this team's losses, you'll find that he's been unlucky with his matchups and should be at least 2-2. Deniz made a trade this past week to acquire a true RB1 in <mark class="hl-player">Chubb</mark>, but I do think he gave up too much in the process, unless <mark class="hl-player">Jeudy</mark> can be a consistent mid-tier WR2. The only hole I can find in this roster is the RB2, because <mark class="hl-player">Wilson Jr.</mark> might become irrelevant in a month, but until then, I think Deniz will start racking up wins if he can face average league opponents.

teams.synopsis: Two straight bad weeks, but Saquon and a healing Herbert say this slide won't last.
teams.blurb: Baylen has taken a massive fall these past two weeks, and I don't know if he'll get back on track. His PA is at the league average (460), meaning he's on average facing an opponent that scores the league average — but he has an upcoming projection below the league average, so if everything goes to plan (which it won't), Baylen will pick up his 3rd straight loss in Week 5. Sticking on the negative side of things, MT looks very injury-prone nowadays and may miss multiple weeks this year for minor things, and Diontae doesn't get looked at by Pickett. On the other hand, Hopkins comes back in a few weeks, Saquon is the best RB in fantasy, and Herbert's injury looks like a thing of the past. Look for this team to add high-value waiver wire players in the upcoming weeks, like Dominic Decoco and Antonio Margheriti.

teams.synopsis: The other side of the Chubb trade — CeeDee looks like a legit WR1 in return.
teams.blurb: Nothing much to say about this team, besides the fact that he got unlucky this past week by playing Brandon. Carmine was the other half of the big trade made this past week that was centered around Chubb — in return, he got <mark class="hl-player">CeeDee</mark>, who is looking like a WR1 with <mark class="hl-player">Cooper Rush</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Dobbins</mark>, who had a great bounce-back game in Week 4. Look for this team to stay at this average ranking until they can prove they're better than the elite fantasy teams.

teams.synopsis: A 3-1 record built entirely on matchups — hasn't cracked 113 points in a single week yet.
teams.blurb: I reluctantly place this team in the top 10, but just out of playoff range — Anthony has yet to score above 113 points in a single week, which is below the average scored by a team per matchup this year (115). Despite finishing as a below-average team every single week, this team is 3-1. That's the reason I simply can't put Kelly higher than 9, even though he has a very good record. Taking a deeper look at his team, you can see he has one of the best WR duos in the league, but is held back by a lackluster flex and a mediocre RB room. Keep an eye on George Pickens, though — he may not have produced up to this point, but with Pickett at the helm, he's been the number-one target in that Steelers offense.

teams.synopsis: The unluckiest schedule in the league — an above-average PF says a turnaround is coming.
teams.blurb: People are probably going to be outraged by this Aidan placement, but hear me out. If Aidan does not win next week, I'll put him at 14, but I still have hope for this team. He's been plagued by unlucky matchups and has the highest PA in the league by a longshot, while still having an above-average PF compared to the rest of the league. Aidan's weaknesses are his WRs, but if they start to produce, he might be able to break the losing streak and avoid a winless season. My advice to Aidan would be to hold out one more week before making a crazy roster change, but if he wants to change something up and upgrade his WRs, look for him to trade <mark class="hl-player">Cook</mark> or <mark class="hl-player">CEH</mark> for a new WR1.

teams.synopsis: A healthy Godwin should stop the slide — Melvin Gordon just needs to fill in behind him.
teams.blurb: Ben's been falling every week, but I think his struggles end this week. <mark class="hl-player">Godwin</mark> is officially healthy and may provide some much-needed WR2 play. His other weaknesses are his flex and TE, but if <mark class="hl-player">Melvin Gordon</mark> can step up and be a low-tier RB2 now that <mark class="hl-player">Javonte</mark> is out, this team will be perfectly fine. Ben doesn't have the highest upcoming projection, but I think he might outperform it and land a top-5 finish this week.

teams.synopsis: Kupp and Cooks keep this team afloat, but shaky RBs cap the ceiling for now.
teams.blurb: I kept Quin at the same spot as last week, because he texted me to put him higher — but I also have other reasons. Geg's team has some legit potential each week with the likes of <mark class="hl-player">Kupp</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Cooks</mark> as his WR duo, but his questionable RBs and flex leave me doubting this team's ability to beat the top teams in the PFFL. Quin didn't make history this week, and that's alright, because he kept the best player in fantasy football away from this team. I don't expect much from this team in Week 5, but I guess it wouldn't shock me if he beat my team.

teams.synopsis: JT's ankle and Patterson's IR stint sunk this ranking — but a fresh trade might fix it fast.
teams.blurb: Got this team at 13 going into Week 5 because of a few things. JT has an ankle injury that should be monitored for the next couple of weeks, along with turf toe, which has been responsible for many RB shortcomings in previous seasons. Another injury causing this team to fall is Patterson being placed on IR, with Chase Edmonds now Gorman's RB2. This team is struggling at the moment, and I'd figure a trade must be done for this team to have a shot at winning in the upcoming weeks. Update: Now that the trade happened, I think this team addressed some holes at the RB position, and I think people are slightly undervaluing the players Gorman received. I think he has a good chance of winning this week and jumping back up the ranks.

teams.synopsis: A win came at the cost of the RB1 — Penny and Mostert need to prove they can fill the void.
teams.blurb: Doesn't get any better for Maney — after an awful showing in Week 3, his team bounced back for a win in Week 4, but at the price of losing his RB1. Cole's problems are his RBs and his TE. I think <mark class="hl-player">Penny</mark> can be good enough to be an average flex play for the rest of the season, and <mark class="hl-player">Mostert</mark> has low-end RB2 potential. <mark class="hl-player">DJ Moore</mark> showed some promise in Week 4, but we've yet to see if it's sustainable. My advice: in the next couple of weeks, look for trade partners willing to part with a reliable RB1/2 — but only if Mostert and Penny can't provide.
